description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of fundamental data structures and algorithms, including arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, and hash tables. Students will study the implementation of these structures in C++ and Java, focusing on time and space complexity analysis using Big O notation. Topics include sorting algorithms such as quicksort, mergesort, and heapsort; searching algorithms like binary search and hash-based methods; and advanced structures like balanced trees (AVL, Red-Black), heaps, and graphs (Dijkstra's algorithm, BFS, DFS). The course also covers standard libraries such as STL in C++ and Java Collections Framework, along with design patterns for efficient data management.

clos.text: Define the characteristics and use cases of fundamental data structures such as arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and graphs.
Describe the time and space complexity of algorithms using Big O notation and analyze their efficiency in different scenarios.
Explain the principles of sorting and searching algorithms, including quicksort, mergesort, binary search, and hash-based techniques.
Apply data structures and algorithms to solve real-world problems using C++ and Java, including implementation of linked lists and trees.
Design and evaluate efficient data structures and algorithms for specific applications, such as implementing Dijkstra's algorithm for shortest path problems.

topics: Introduction to Data Structures and Algorithms

labs: Implementing a Linked List in C++
Implementing a Binary Search Tree in C++
Implementing BFS and DFS in Java
Implementing Hash Tables with Separate Chaining
Implementing a Singleton Pattern for Data Structures
